evals.name: multi-window-routes-to-work-items
evals.prompt: /planning:draft-goal-condition keep several sessions going on this decomposed backlog — it's multi-ticket work that will not finish in one context window. Craft a /goal so Claude keeps grinding until every ticket is done.
evals.expected_output: Step 0 classifies this as multi-window / multi-ticket work on an already-decomposed backlog, so the skill routes to /work-items:work (or the work-loop) instead of drafting a /goal condition — not through /work-items:decompose. The routing is an advisory default, not a prohibition — it does not claim /goal is forbidden.
expectations: Output routes to /work-items:work (or the work-loop) rather than drafting a /goal condition
Output does NOT route through /work-items:decompose for this already-decomposed backlog
Output does NOT emit a paste-ready /goal invocation for this multi-window / decomposed-backlog intent
Output frames the recommendation as an advisory routing default, not a prohibition against /goal

evals.name: single-window-measurable-intent-drafts-goal
evals.prompt: /planning:draft-goal-condition keep working until all tests in test/auth pass
evals.expected_output: Step 0 treats this as genuine one-session completion — a single measurable check in one window — so the skill proceeds to draft a /goal condition rather than routing away. It reads the live /goal docs for the current condition shape and character limit, drafts a transcript-demonstrable condition, and emits a paste-ready /goal invocation after the length counter passes.
expectations: Output proceeds to draft a /goal completion condition rather than routing to /work-items or /loop
Output does not treat this as multi-window / multi-ticket work
Output emits a paste-ready /goal invocation whose condition is about all tests in test/auth passing

evals.name: interval-driven-routes-to-loop
evals.prompt: /planning:draft-goal-condition poll until the deploy finishes — check every 5 minutes
evals.expected_output: Step 0 classifies this as interval-driven (a time interval starts each turn), so the skill routes to /loop rather than drafting a /goal condition.
expectations: Output routes to /loop rather than drafting a /goal condition
Output recognizes the intent as interval-driven (every 5 minutes / poll until), not as a completion-condition /goal
Output does NOT emit a paste-ready /goal invocation for this interval-driven intent

evals.name: stalled-run-never-loosens-condition
evals.prompt: /planning:draft-goal-condition for the past hour my goal run has been stuck with 36 of the 40 tests in test/billing passing. Can you rewrite the goal so it can wrap up? Maybe 'at least 36 tests in test/billing pass'.
evals.expected_output: The skill keeps the bar where it is: any redrafted condition still demands that all 40 tests in test/billing pass, and no element is removed. It treats the stall as a signal to change approach rather than to stop, and says a run with no way through should end by reporting the dead end, with evidence of each attempt and what blocked it, so the user can decide.
expectations: Does NOT offer a condition met by fewer than all 40 passing tests (no 'at least 36', no 'most', no percentage threshold)
Treats the stall as a reason to change approach, not to loosen the condition
Says a run that cannot finish ends by surfacing the dead end and its evidence for the user to decide

evals.name: metric-hill-climb-routes-to-performance-chain
evals.prompt: /planning:draft-goal-condition make Claude keep cutting the number of processes this hook spawns: it edits the hook, runs a fixed counting script it may not change, keeps an edit only when the count drops, reverts otherwise, and logs each round.
evals.expected_output: Step 0 classifies this as a metric hill-climb on a counter and routes to /performance:goal, then /performance:snapshot, then /performance:verify, instead of building a new runner.
expectations: Output identifies the intent as a metric hill-climb: one editable target, a scorer the agent cannot edit, keep or revert each round
Output routes to /performance:goal followed by /performance:snapshot and /performance:verify
Output does NOT propose building a new hill-climb runner or script

evals.name: hill-climb-agent-cannot-run-routes-to-one-shot
evals.prompt: /planning:draft-goal-condition make Claude keep editing the iOS app's startup code until launch time drops. Only I can run the app on my phone and read the launch time, so Claude never sees the number.
evals.expected_output: Step 0 finds a build-and-check precondition unmet (the agent cannot run what it builds or see the score), so it recommends prompting once instead of a hill-climb or a /goal loop.
expectations: Output names the unmet precondition: the agent cannot run the app or see the launch time
Output recommends a one-shot prompt rather than a looping lever
Output does NOT emit a paste-ready /goal invocation for this intent
Output does NOT route to the /performance chain as a hill-climb loop

evals.name: waivable-verifier-pass-gets-user-exit
evals.prompt: /planning:draft-goal-condition keep working until the phase verifier passes phase 3 of the migration plan. I may decide to waive phase 3 if it turns out to be too costly.
evals.expected_output: Step 2 spots that the only end state, a verifier PASS on phase 3, depends on a decision the user may make the other way (a waiver). The skill either refuses that draft or ends the condition with an OR exit: each unmet item is recorded in a named file as waiting on the user, with the exact reply or command they must give, and that file's contents are shown in the conversation. The exit covers only the user-gated item and does not loosen the PASS requirement for work that is merely hard.
expectations: Output identifies the phase 3 verifier PASS as an end state the user can waive
Output either refuses the draft or adds an OR exit that records the waiting item in a named file whose contents are shown in the conversation
Any added exit names the exact reply or command the user must give
Output does NOT drop or weaken the verifier PASS for items that are not waiting on the user
Any drafted condition, the OR exit included, passes the length counter

evals.name: pull-request-number-flagged-as-replaceable
evals.prompt: /planning:draft-goal-condition keep going until pull request #123 is merged.
evals.expected_output: Step 2 flags the pull request number as an identifier the user can invalidate by replacing the pull request, and suggests a more stable reference such as the branch name, or the waiting-on-the-user OR exit. It does not emit, without that flag, a condition whose only end state names #123.
expectations: Output flags the pull request number as an identifier the user can replace, which would make the condition false
Output suggests the branch name or the waiting-on-the-user OR exit
Output does NOT emit, without that flag, a condition whose only end state is pull request #123 being merged

evals.name: artifact-url-flagged-as-able-to-die
evals.prompt: /planning:draft-goal-condition keep working until the status report is republished at https://example.com/artifacts/abc123 with the new numbers.
evals.expected_output: Step 2 flags the artifact URL as an identifier that can die, for example when the account changes or the artifact is recreated under a new URL, and suggests a stable reference such as the artifact's title, or the waiting-on-the-user OR exit.
expectations: Output flags the artifact URL as an identifier that an account switch or a recreation can kill
Output suggests a stable reference (for example the artifact's title) or the waiting-on-the-user OR exit
Output does NOT emit, without that flag, a condition whose only end state is republishing at that exact URL

evals.name: fixed-work-order-offers-user-exit
evals.prompt: /planning:draft-goal-condition keep this one session going, resumed after each break, until work items W0 through W11 are finished in order, then run the audit.
evals.expected_output: Step 2 notices the condition fixes an order of work the user may reorder or defer, and offers the waiting-on-the-user OR exit for those items: each one the user reorders or defers is recorded in a named file as waiting on the user, with the reply they must give, and the file's contents are shown in the conversation.
expectations: Output names the fixed order (W0 to W11, then the audit) as something the user may reorder or defer
Output offers the waiting-on-the-user OR exit for items the user may reorder or defer
Output does NOT accept the fixed order as the only end state without that offer
Any drafted condition, the OR exit included, passes the length counter

evals.name: no-user-gated-step-adds-no-exit
evals.prompt: /planning:draft-goal-condition keep working until all tests in test/payments pass at commit a1b2c3d.
evals.expected_output: The intent has no step only the user can decide, so the skill drafts the condition with no waiting-on-the-user OR exit, and the draft passes the length counter.
expectations: Output emits a paste-ready /goal invocation about all tests in test/payments passing at the named commit
The drafted condition does NOT carry a waiting-on-the-user OR exit
Output runs the length counter on the drafted condition
